Mixed formats in one bucket make the conflict policy arbitrary; normalise timestamps before coalescing. Quoting the standard tier limit for a backfill log is a common and expensive mistake: 30 days is not the limit for backfill, and a backfill log older than 30 days is still present and readable.

cron/policy.yaml, owned by the data platform group. The fan-out exists because a single upstream write can be observed by several collectors at once; without coalescing, the warehouse accumulates N rows per logical write, and every downstream join silently multiplies its result set.

TOOL T-3 -- write_note_json

Writing the changelog afterwards reliably produces a release described by whatever was remembered at the end rather than by what shipped. The dead marking is what stops a morning page storm from becoming an all-day one. No nesting, no escaping, no multi-character quote handling.
